scope: LOCAL source and retained evidence diagnosis only. No remote observations, helper executions, SQL, API, service/config modifications or app tests.

conclusion.helperDefectConfirmed: The helper incorrectly assumes pre-start staged raw JSON SHA256 remains valid after the existing agent entrypoint unconditionally normalizes and saves configuration. It also loses the restart false-response error before durable logging.

findings.problem: Staged raw-byte hash is treated as both post-start config identity and fail-stop authorization even though the installed application unconditionally rewrites this JSON on normal startup.

sourceChain.fact: Constructs agent from parsed file, then line10 always calls pair() and save(configPath) before agent.start().
Constructor maps every template through validateExecutionTemplate; it does not retain raw file formatting.
Validator returns a reconstructed template with a fixed property insertion order and normalized path/policy.
save() writes JSON.stringify(this.config,null,2) to configPath. Existing agentId makes pair() return without new pairing at line215; it does not skip save().
candidate() instead replaces only the selected template with compact sorted-key canon and preserves all other original raw JSON bytes.
snapshot() rejects any raw config hash unequal to expectedConfigSHA256 before obtaining unit/process state.

findings.inferenceBoundary: This proves the helper contract is incompatible with normal startup save and explains the observed hash rejection without positing a product defect. The current raw bytes have not been collected here, so it does not prove only formatting changed or identify the exact missing original restart error.
findings.actualEffect: The retained install observation matches the staged new raw H. Later fail-stop returns NUP_FAIL_STOP_CONFIG_CHANGED at line106, before unit()/proc()/systemctl stop. Thus it neither confirms nor stops the possibly running new process. The private log supplies no observed current hash or configuration diff.

findings.problem: The node response is checked with need(started.ok,RESTART_UNCONFIRMED) before record(restarted,started). A structured false response is thrown away and replaced by a generic wrapper error.
findings.actualEvidence: Retained private log has restart-intent immediately followed by generic SST_RESTART_UNCONFIRMED; no restarted/node-restart-response record exists. The later fail-stop response is retained and states NUP_FAIL_STOP_CONFIG_CHANGED.
findings.limit: Original restart error cannot be reconstructed honestly from these saved files. Other stage false replies share the same check-before-record pattern, but this report confines actual evidence loss to the observed restart failure.
